RESPONSE TO REQUEST FOR INFORMATION

RFI No. W52P1J-26-R-0147 — Enterprise Data Analytics and AI Modernization Services

Submitted to: U.S. Army Program Executive Office, Enterprise Information Systems (PEO EIS)

Submitted by: Meridian Federal Solutions, LLC

Submission Date: July 17, 2026 | Response Valid Through: October 15, 2026

CAGE Code: 8KDR4 | UEI: MFSLLC29XKT7 | NAICS: 541512, 541511, 518210

1. Executive Summary

Meridian Federal Solutions, LLC (Meridian) is pleased to respond to RFI No. W52P1J-26-R-0147 issued by PEO EIS on June 12, 2026, seeking industry input on Enterprise Data Analytics and AI Modernization Services. Meridian is a CMMI-DEV Maturity Level 3 appraised, ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 27001:2022 certified small business headquartered in Arlington, Virginia, with 480 employees supporting federal civilian and defense customers.

Meridian brings directly relevant experience delivering secure, production-grade AI platforms at scale, including a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) knowledge platform serving more than 12,000 users at the Department of Veterans Affairs and a predictive logistics analytics capability for U.S. Transportation Command processing 4.2 billion records daily. Our recommended approach centers on a cloud-native, containerized architecture deployed to the Army cArmy environment at Impact Level 5 (IL5), leveraging a mission-tuned large language model gateway with human-in-the-loop guardrails.

We estimate that a full-scale implementation of the capabilities described in the RFI can reach Initial Operating Capability (IOC) within 9 months of award and Full Operating Capability (FOC) within 18 months, at a rough order of magnitude (ROM) of $34M–$42M over a five-year period of performance.

3. Understanding of the Requirement

Based on our reading of the RFI and the accompanying draft Performance Work Statement (PWS), PEO EIS seeks industry feedback on five capability areas: (1) enterprise data mesh and governance; (2) AI/ML model development, deployment, and monitoring (MLOps); (3) retrieval-augmented generation over classified and unclassified corpora; (4) legacy analytics migration from on-premises Oracle and SAS environments; and (5) workforce enablement and AI literacy training.

The central technical challenge is not model selection but data readiness: our experience across 14 federal AI programs indicates that 70–80% of program effort is consumed by data ingestion, entity resolution, labeling, and access control alignment. Any acquisition strategy should therefore weight data engineering and governance at least as heavily as model capability.

4. Recommended Technical Approach

4.1 Reference Architecture

Meridian recommends a layered, vendor-agnostic architecture deployed on AWS GovCloud (IL5) with portability to Azure Government. The stack comprises Kubernetes (EKS) orchestration, an event-driven ingestion layer built on Kafka and AWS Glue, a lakehouse storage tier (S3 + Apache Iceberg), a vector store (OpenSearch with k-NN, with pgvector as a lightweight alternative for smaller enclaves), and an LLM gateway supporting Claude, GPT, and open-weight models behind a single policy enforcement point.

4.2 RAG Pipeline

Ingestion & chunking: format-aware parsers for DOCX, PDF, PPTX, and HTML with semantic chunking at 512–1,024 tokens and 15% overlap, preserving section hierarchy as metadata.

Hybrid retrieval: BM25 + dense embeddings with reciprocal rank fusion, followed by a cross-encoder re-ranking stage; measured 23-point improvement in recall@10 over dense-only retrieval on VA benchmark corpora.

Access-aware retrieval: row- and document-level security trimming at query time using attribute-based access control (ABAC) claims propagated from ICAM.

Grounded generation: citation-forced prompting with answerability classification; ungrounded responses are suppressed and routed to a human review queue.

Evaluation: automated regression harness measuring faithfulness, answer relevance, and context precision on a 1,200-item gold set, executed on every index or prompt change.

4.3 Security and Compliance

All components align to NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 moderate/high baselines and NIST AI RMF 1.0. Meridian operates two FedRAMP High authorized SaaS offerings and has achieved Authority to Operate (ATO) under RMF at six DoD components, with a median time-to-ATO of 5.5 months using our pre-built OSCAL control inheritance packages.

11 DoD ATOs delivered; OSCAL automation SME; TS.

7. Management and Staffing Approach

Meridian recommends a scaled agile construct: a core platform team of 12 FTEs (IOC phase) growing to three mission-aligned pods of 6–8 FTEs each at FOC, governed by a lightweight Program Increment cadence of 10-week increments. We staff 85% of positions with current employees at award and maintain a cleared bench of 40+ engineers. Attrition on our federal AI programs averaged 6.8% in FY2025 against an industry benchmark of 13.2%.

8. Rough Order of Magnitude and Assumptions

Labor Category

ROM Rate (hr)

Basis

DevSecOps Engineer

$156

GSA MAS SIN 54151S

Cloud Infrastructure (ODC)

$1.4M–$1.9M / yr

AWS GovCloud, IL5, 3-env topology

Assumes Government-furnished ICAM integration endpoints and sponsorship for IL5 ATO reciprocity.

ROM excludes LLM inference consumption above 500M tokens/month; overage priced at cost + 8% handling.

Assumes hybrid workplace with 40% on-site presence at Fort Belvoir, VA.

9. Responses to Specific RFI Questions

Q1. What contract type do you recommend and why?

A hybrid structure: FFP for platform sustainment CLINs, T&M for exploratory AI use-case CLINs, and a cost-reimbursable CLIN for cloud consumption. This isolates consumption risk from delivery risk and avoids padding FFP prices with cloud contingency.

Q2. Should the Government pursue a single award or multiple award IDIQ?

Multiple award (3–5 awardees) with a common platform baseline defined by the Government preserves competition at the task order level while preventing platform fragmentation. We recommend an on-ramp provision at option year 2.

Q3. What is a realistic timeline for IOC?

Nine months, contingent on Government-furnished data access within 60 days of award. The critical path is historically ATO and data-sharing agreements, not engineering.

10. Points of Contact

Primary: Daniel Okafor, Vice President of Growth — dokafor@meridianfs.com — (703) 555-0182

Technical: Dr. Marcus Webb, Chief AI Architect — mwebb@meridianfs.com — (703) 555-0147

Contracts: Elena Vasquez, Director of Contracts — evasquez@meridianfs.com — (703) 555-0119

This response contains no proprietary pricing commitments and is provided for planning purposes only. Meridian requests notification of any Industry Day associated with this requirement.
